items.title: Record anchor files on derived finding-signals
items.context: Add optional anchorFiles?: string[] to FindingSignal in core/experience-layer-types.ts (forward-compat, capped) and populate it in core/finding-signals.ts by accumulating finding.files (union, sorted, capped by a new MAX_ANCHOR_FILES constant mirroring MAX_EXAMPLES). Pure-leaf discipline unchanged.
items.userSees: Derived signals now carry the concrete file paths their composing findings referenced.

happy.desc: deriveFindingSignals with findings that have non-empty files[] -> resulting FindingSignal has anchorFiles populated as sorted union of all finding.files; WHY: confirms the core data flow from finding.files to anchorFiles
deriveFindingSignals with findings that have empty/missing files[] -> resulting FindingSignal has no anchorFiles field (omitted, not empty array); WHY: confirms clean output for legacy signals

edge.desc: deriveFindingSignals with more distinct files across findings than MAX_ANCHOR_FILES -> anchorFiles is capped at MAX_ANCHOR_FILES length, sorted, no duplicates; WHY: boundary guard against unbounded growth
deriveFindingSignals with a single finding whose files contains duplicates -> anchorFiles is deduplicated; WHY: ensures Set-based dedup works
localSignature key computation unchanged after anchorFiles addition -> signals with identical category/signatureTag/fileKind/lifecyclePhase still aggregate together; WHY: guards excludes constraint

adversarial.desc: deriveFindingSignals with finding.files containing non-string values (numbers, null, objects) -> anchorFiles only includes valid strings; WHY: real findings can have malformed data
signalScore and support values are identical before and after anchorFiles addition for same input -> no regression to scoring math; WHY: guards the excludes constraint that scoring is unchanged
anchorFiles contains only string-filtered entries from finding.files (same filter as toSourceFinding) -> no path traversal sequences or empty strings leak through; WHY: adversarial input sanitation

items.title: Pure re-validation leaf (revalidateSignals + computeValidRate)
items.context: New core/experience-revalidation.ts importing only ./experience-layer-types.js. revalidateSignals(cache, fileExists) classifies each signal valid(>=1 anchor present)/stale(all anchors gone)/unanchored(no anchorFiles); computeValidRate aggregates total/anchored/valid/stale/unanchored + validRate + driftRate. fileExists is injected (no fs/git in the leaf).
items.userSees: A deterministic, fs-free function that turns signals + a HEAD predicate into a valid-rate report.
excludes: No filesystem or git access in the leaf

happy.desc: revalidateSignals with 3 signals (1 has all anchors present, 1 has all anchors gone, 1 has no anchorFiles) -> returns validity array with states valid/stale/unanchored respectively; WHY: covers all three classification branches

computeValidRate on [2 valid, 1 stale, 1 unanchored] -> total=4, anchored=3, valid=2, stale=1, unanchored=1, validRate=2/3, driftRate=1/3; WHY: confirms the ANCHORED-ONLY denominator formula and all counter fields
revalidateSignals with a signal where anchorFiles has 5 files, 1 present and 4 missing -> state is valid (not stale); WHY: confirms >=1 anchor present threshold

edge.desc: computeValidRate with zero anchored signals (all unanchored) -> validRate=0, driftRate=0, never NaN; WHY: guards the zero-denominator edge case that would produce NaN without the ternary guard
computeValidRate with empty validity array -> total=0, anchored=0, validRate=0, driftRate=0; WHY: empty-input boundary
revalidateSignals with signal whose anchorFiles is empty array [] -> classified as unanchored (same as absent); WHY: empty array is a degenerate form of no-anchor
computeValidRate with all valid signals (zero stale) -> driftRate=0, validRate=1.0; WHY: confirms perfect health scenario

adversarial.desc: core/experience-revalidation.ts imports ONLY ./experience-layer-types.js (no node:fs, no child_process, no node:path) -> static import analysis confirms leaf purity; WHY: the leaf must never do I/O itself, fileExists is injected

revalidateSignals called with fileExists that throws on certain paths -> exception propagates (not silently swallowed); WHY: callers must handle fs errors at the handler layer, not inside the pure leaf

computeValidRate with a single stale signal among 100 unanchored -> anchored=1, stale=1, driftRate=1.0, not diluted by unanchored count; WHY: adversarial scenario where unanchored signals could dilute the denominator if the formula is wrong

revalidateSignals with duplicate file paths in anchorFiles -> present/missing partition still correct (no double-counting); WHY: if anchorFiles somehow has duplicates, classification must be consistent

items.title: Read-only learning_validate handler + CLI command
items.context: New handlers/learning-validate.ts: build fileExists from `git ls-tree -r --name-only -z HEAD` (own execFileSync, do NOT modify evidence-freshness.ts), derive signals via deriveFindingSignalsFromStore(ctx.store) WITHOUT projectRoot (no persist), run the leaf, render a human report and --json. Optional --story to restrict. Register in registry.ts + cli-engine.ts. Files no findings, touches no gate, writes nothing.
items.userSees: Running `lattice learning_validate` prints valid-rate and drift-rate over the live finding history; `--json` emits the machine-readable report.

happy.desc: lattice learning_validate in a repo with finding history -> prints human-readable report containing valid-rate and drift-rate lines; WHY: confirms the core user-facing output
lattice learning_validate --json -> outputs valid JSON with total/anchored/valid/stale/unanchored/validRate/driftRate fields; WHY: confirms machine-readable output path
lattice learning_validate --story B-xxxx -> restricts derivation to that story only; WHY: confirms the optional story filter works
learning_validate registered in cli-engine.ts with schema {json?: boolean, story?: string} -> command is discoverable and schema matches; WHY: confirms CLI wiring
learning_validate registered in registry.ts via createLearningValidateHandlers -> handler is callable; WHY: confirms handler registration

edge.desc: lattice learning_validate in a repo with no finding history (empty store) -> prints valid-rate 0 / drift-rate 0, does not crash; WHY: empty-store boundary

lattice learning_validate when git ls-tree HEAD fails (not a git repo or empty repo) -> treats file set as empty (all anchored signals become stale), does not crash; WHY: confirms the try/catch fallback in fileExists construction
learning_validate appears in core/config.ts DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS wildcard list -> command is allowed in all phases; WHY: confirms phase-access registration
learning_validate has command-policy entry with status=supported, ownershipClass=readOnly, allowedPhases=all, destructiveRisk=none -> policy metadata correct; WHY: confirms read-only classification

adversarial.desc: after running lattice learning_validate, no files in .lattice/ are modified (finding-signals.json not written, no gate touched, no findings added) -> verify via git diff or file stat; WHY: the handler must NOT persist anything -- deriveFindingSignalsFromStore called WITHOUT projectRoot

handler does NOT call finding_add, advisory_add, or any gate registration function -> static analysis of handlers/learning-validate.ts confirms no write/finding/gate imports; WHY: adversarial check that read-only contract is honored
handler builds its own execFileSync for git ls-tree (does NOT import or modify evidence-freshness.ts) -> static import analysis; WHY: the plan explicitly forbids modifying evidence-freshness.ts
lattice learning_validate with --story pointing to a nonexistent story ID -> graceful handling (empty derivation, not a crash); WHY: adversarial invalid input

items.title: Smoke test + npm script + verifier
items.context: Hermetic smoke for the pure leaf (synthetic signals + injected fileExists asserting validRate/driftRate) plus a CLI smoke that runs learning_validate on a temp store and asserts a valid-rate line. Wire an npm script and a committed verify-*.mjs that builds + runs the smokes and prints TOTAL/PASS/FAIL.
items.userSees: npm smoke passes and the verifier prints PASS for the re-validation metric.
excludes: No reliance on real repo state in the hermetic leaf test
